subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Seoul's Café Explosion
description: A short lesson to help you apply Seoul's Café Explosion.

hook.text: South Korea has more cafés per capita than almost any country. Seoul alone has over 18,000 coffee shops.

buildup.text: Korean café culture exploded in the 2010s—driven by social media, aesthetics, and the desire for 'third places.'

discovery.text: Many Korean cafés are architectural statements—converted warehouses, greenhouses, and minimalist concrete cubes.

twist.text: Competition is brutal. The average Korean café survives only 3 years. Thousands open and close annually.

climax.text: Despite high turnover, the culture thrives. Koreans spend more on café visits per person than any other nationality.

punchline.text: 18,000 cafés and counting. Seoul runs on aesthetics and espresso.

quiz.question: What drives South Korea's massive café culture?
options: Social media, aesthetics, and desire for beautiful 'third places'

details.summary: Seoul has more cafes per capita than almost any city in the world, with over 18,000 coffee shops. Korean cafe culture blends third-wave quality with Instagram aesthetics, innovative menu concepts, and competitive coffee competitions. Korea has become one of the world's most dynamic coffee markets.
details.whyItMatters: Seoul's cafe scene demonstrates how rapidly coffee culture can evolve in a traditionally tea-drinking country, driven by youth culture and social media.
takeaways: Seoul has over 18,000 coffee shops across the city
Korean cafe culture blends quality with aesthetic innovation
South Korea is among the world's fastest-growing coffee markets

faq.question: Why did South Korea become so obsessed with cafes?
faq.answer: Cultural factors include small apartments that push socializing into public spaces, competitive youth culture that embraced Western trends, social media driving cafe aesthetics, and a strong startup culture of cafe entrepreneurs. Cafes became study rooms, date spots, and status symbols.

faq.question: What makes Korean cafe culture unique?
faq.answer: Korean cafes push design boundaries with themed interiors, multi-story buildings, and destination concepts. Menu innovation is constant, blending coffee with desserts and local flavors. Korea also has a world-class competition barista scene and imports some of the finest beans available.
